accepted.s: The Delimitation Order, 2008, presently governing the constituencies of Andhra Pradesh was based on which Census and Commission combination?
o: 1991 Census and Delimitation Commission constituted in 2002
2001 Census and Delimitation Commission constituted in 2008
2011 Census and Delimitation Commission constituted in 2002
2001 Census and Delimitation Commission constituted in 2002
accepted.x: The Delimitation Order, 2008 was based on the 2001 Census and the Delimitation Commission constituted in 2002.
accepted.tq: Separate the Census year from the year of the Commission.
accepted.sec: Delimitation in AP - Delimitation Order 2008, AP Reorganisation Act 2014

accepted.s: After the reorganisation of Andhra Pradesh, the number of Assembly and Lok Sabha constituencies presently governed by the Delimitation Order, 2008 is respectively:
accepted.x: The present Andhra Pradesh has 175 Assembly constituencies and 25 Lok Sabha constituencies under the Delimitation Order, 2008 after the 2014 reorganisation.
accepted.tq: Match the two figures as a constituency pair.
accepted.sec: Delimitation in AP - Delimitation Order 2008, AP Reorganisation Act 2014

accepted.s: Section 26 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 provided for increasing the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly seats from 175 to:
accepted.x: Section 26 envisaged increasing the Andhra Pradesh Assembly strength from 175 to 225, subject to Article 170.
accepted.tq: Check the proposed figure against the existing strength.
accepted.sec: Delimitation in AP - Delimitation Order 2008, AP Reorganisation Act 2014

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the proposed increase in Assembly seats under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014:
1. Andhra Pradesh Assembly seats were proposed to increase from 175 to 225.
2. Telangana Assembly seats were proposed to increase from 119 to 153.
3. The increase operates independently of Article 170 of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the proposal is subject to Article 170.
accepted.tq: Reject the statement that removes an expressly stated constitutional condition.
accepted.sec: Delimitation in AP - Delimitation Order 2008, AP Reorganisation Act 2014

accepted.s: Article 170(3) of the Constitution freezes the number of Assembly seats until:
accepted.x: Article 170(3) freezes Assembly numbers until the first Census after 2026. An earlier increase would require a constitutional amendment.
accepted.tq: Focus on the exact constitutional time reference.
accepted.sec: Delimitation in AP - Delimitation Order 2008, AP Reorganisation Act 2014

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Article 325 provides for one general electoral roll and prohibits exclusion on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex. Article 324 concerns the Election Commission, Article 326 adult suffrage, and Article 329 court-related bars.
accepted.tq: Use the Article-subject pairing rather than relying on familiar article numbers.
accepted.sec: Electoral provisions in the Constitution - Part XV, Articles 324-329

accepted.s: Which Article of the Constitution vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission of India?
accepted.x: Article 324 vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission of India.
accepted.tq: Identify the constitutional provision from its distinctive power.
accepted.sec: Electoral provisions in the Constitution - Part XV, Articles 324-329

accepted.s: Under Article 329, which of the following is correct?
o: Only the Election Commission can decide disputes concerning delimitation laws.
Elections can be challenged only by an election petition, while delimitation laws are barred from being questioned in court.
Delimitation laws may be questioned in any subordinate court.
All election disputes may be directly challenged before any court before polling begins.
accepted.x: Article 329 bars courts from questioning delimitation laws and provides that an election may be challenged only through an election petition.
accepted.tq: Choose the option preserving both limbs of the constitutional bar.
accepted.sec: Electoral provisions in the Constitution - Part XV, Articles 324-329

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the qualifying dates for revision of electoral rolls?
accepted.x: The four qualifying dates are 1 January, 1 April, 1 July and 1 October. 1 December is not a qualifying date.
accepted.tq: Find the date outside the four-date set.
accepted.sec: Electoral rolls - qualifying dates, overseas electors, revisions

accepted.s: The four qualifying dates for enrolment in electoral rolls, introduced through the Election Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021, are:
accepted.x: The qualifying dates are 1 January, 1 April, 1 July and 1 October.
accepted.tq: Recall the complete four-date sequence rather than one isolated date.
accepted.sec: Electoral rolls - qualifying dates, overseas electors, revisions

accepted.s: An overseas Indian elector may enrol in the electoral roll at:
o: the address of the Indian embassy in the foreign country
any address selected by the elector
the last place of employment in India בלבד
the address of the Indian passport
accepted.x: Under Section 20A of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, an overseas elector may enrol at the address given in the Indian passport.
accepted.tq: Apply the special registration rule to the overseas-elector scenario.
accepted.sec: Electoral rolls - qualifying dates, overseas electors, revisions

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls?
o: It rebuilds the electoral roll comprehensively.
It is undertaken only after a general election result.
It is conducted only for overseas electors.
It is an annual summary correction without rebuilding the roll.
accepted.x: A Special Intensive Revision rebuilds the electoral roll, whereas summary revision is conducted annually.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the comprehensive revision from the routine annual revision.
accepted.sec: Electoral rolls - qualifying dates, overseas electors, revisions

accepted.s: An exit poll is best described as:
o: A survey conducted before the election notification to assess voter intention
A poll of voters taken immediately after they leave the polling station
A survey conducted only among political party workers
A statistical report prepared after the declaration of results
accepted.x: An exit poll is conducted among voters immediately after they leave the polling station; it is different from an opinion poll.
accepted.tq: Separate the timing of an exit poll from that of an opinion poll.
accepted.sec: Exit polls and opinion polls - Section 126A

accepted.s: Under Section 126A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the prohibition on conducting or publishing exit polls extends from:
o: 48 hours before the first phase until the close of the last phase
the issue of the election notification until the declaration of results
the first nomination date until the last counting day
the start of polling in the first phase until half an hour after the close of polling in the last phase
accepted.x: Section 126A prohibits conducting or publishing exit polls from the commencement of polling in the first phase until half an hour after polling closes in the last phase.
accepted.tq: Track both the starting point and the precise end point.
accepted.sec: Exit polls and opinion polls - Section 126A

accepted.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the restrictions on opinion polls and exit polls?
o: Opinion polls are barred for 48 hours before the close of poll, whereas Section 126A covers exit polls across multi-phase polling.
Exit polls are barred only for 48 hours before the close of poll, whereas opinion polls are barred from the first phase.
Both are barred only after the declaration of results.
Neither is subject to a statutory restriction.
accepted.x: Opinion polls are barred during the 48 hours before the close of poll under Section 126, while Section 126A governs the longer phase-to-phase restriction on exit polls.
accepted.tq: Compare the two restrictions by both subject and time period.
accepted.sec: Exit polls and opinion polls - Section 126A

accepted.s: The formula for election indelible ink is associated with the:
accepted.x: The formula for the indelible ink comes from the National Physical Laboratory, while Mysore Paints and Varnish Limited manufactures it.
accepted.tq: Use the manufacturer-versus-formula distinction.
accepted.sec: Indelible ink - manufacturer, finger, composition

accepted.s: Indelible ink is ordinarily applied to the:
accepted.x: Election indelible ink is applied to the left forefinger.
accepted.tq: Recall the precise finger rather than the general hand.
accepted.sec: Indelible ink - manufacturer, finger, composition

accepted.s: The key chemical responsible for the indelible character of election ink is:
accepted.x: Silver nitrate is the key chemical in election indelible ink.
accepted.tq: Identify the distinctive chemical component.
accepted.sec: Indelible ink - manufacturer, finger, composition

accepted.s: Indelible ink was first used in the Indian general election of:
accepted.x: Indelible ink was first used in the 1962 general election. The claim that it was first used in Mysore in 1960 is incorrect.
accepted.tq: Reject the nearby but incorrect preliminary-use year.
accepted.sec: Indelible ink - manufacturer, finger, composition

accepted.s: For a Lok Sabha election, the notification commencing the election process is issued by the:
o: Governor, on the recommendation of the Election Commission
President, on the recommendation of the Election Commission
Chief Election Commissioner, without executive recommendation
Union Home Minister, on the recommendation of the President
accepted.x: Under Section 14 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the President issues the notification for a Lok Sabha election on the Election Commission's recommendation.
accepted.tq: Ask which constitutional authority issues the notification at Union level.
accepted.sec: Commencement of the election process - Sections 14 and 15 RPA

accepted.s: For an Assembly election, the notification commencing the election process is issued by the:
accepted.x: Under Section 15 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the Governor issues the notification for a State Assembly election on the Election Commission's recommendation.
accepted.tq: Match the level of election with the issuing authority and section.
accepted.sec: Commencement of the election process - Sections 14 and 15 RPA

accepted.s: Which authority fixes the election schedule and nomination dates?
accepted.x: The Election Commission fixes the election schedule and nomination dates, while the President or Governor issues the formal notification as applicable.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the authority fixing the schedule from the authority issuing the notification.
accepted.sec: Commencement of the election process - Sections 14 and 15 RPA

accepted.s: A by-election to fill a casual vacancy is ordinarily required to be held within:
accepted.x: A by-election is ordinarily held within six months of a vacancy, subject to the stated exceptions.
accepted.tq: Recall the statutory time limit before considering exceptions.
accepted.sec: Commencement of the election process - Sections 14 and 15 RPA

accepted.s: The six-month requirement for a by-election does NOT apply when:
o: the vacancy occurs in a reserved constituency
the election is held during the monsoon season
the constituency has more than one polling station
the remaining term is under one year or the Election Commission certifies difficulty after consulting the Centre
accepted.x: The exceptions are where the remaining term is less than one year or the Election Commission, after consulting the Central Government, certifies difficulty in holding the election.
accepted.tq: Look for the option containing both statutory exceptions.
accepted.sec: Commencement of the election process - Sections 14 and 15 RPA

accepted.s: Which of the following persons is eligible for the absentee-voter postal ballot category on the basis of age?
o: A citizen aged 90 years or above only
A citizen aged 80 years or above
A citizen aged 75 years or above
A citizen aged 85 years or above
accepted.x: The senior-citizen threshold for the absentee-voter postal ballot category is 85 years or above, raised from 80 years.
accepted.tq: Notice the revised threshold rather than the former age limit.
accepted.sec: Postal ballot and home voting - eligible categories and age

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the listed categories eligible for postal ballot or home voting?
o: All private-sector employees irrespective of election duty
Persons with benchmark disability of 40 per cent or more
accepted.x: The listed categories include senior citizens aged 85 or above, persons with benchmark disability of 40 per cent or more, essential-service staff on duty, service voters, election-duty electors and persons under preventive detention.
accepted.tq: Identify the overbroad category that is not recognised in the specified list.
accepted.sec: Postal ballot and home voting - eligible categories and age

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the election officer's role?
o: Returning Officer — conducts the poll in a constituency and declares the result
District Election Officer — manufactures indelible ink
Chief Electoral Officer — issues election petitions
Electoral Registration Officer — appoints the Election Commission
accepted.x: The Returning Officer conducts the poll in a constituency and declares the result. The other roles are incorrectly assigned.
accepted.tq: Start with the officer whose constituency-level function is distinctive.
accepted.sec: Election machinery - CEO, DEO, Returning Officer, observers

accepted.s: The District Election Officer is generally the:
accepted.x: At the district level, the District Election Officer is usually the Collector.
accepted.tq: Match the district-level election designation with the usual administrative office.
accepted.sec: Election machinery - CEO, DEO, Returning Officer, observers

accepted.s: Under Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, expense accounts are received within 30 days by the:
accepted.x: The District Election Officer receives election expense accounts within 30 days under Section 78.
accepted.tq: Pair the statutory section with the responsible officer.
accepted.sec: Election machinery - CEO, DEO, Returning Officer, observers

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a category of observer appointed by the Election Commission under Section 20B?
accepted.x: The listed observer categories are general, police and expenditure observers. Judicial observer is not among them.
accepted.tq: Find the role outside the three-member observer set.
accepted.sec: Election machinery - CEO, DEO, Returning Officer, observers

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about election machinery:
1. The Chief Electoral Officer assists the Election Commission in each State or Union Territory.
2. Electoral Registration Officers and Booth Level Officers are associated with electoral rolls.
3. Booth Level Officers now carry standard photo identity cards.
4. The Election Commission has no control over officers deployed on poll duty.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the Election Commission controls officers on poll duty and may transfer them or act against partisan conduct.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute statement denying the Election Commission's supervisory control.
accepted.sec: Election machinery - CEO, DEO, Returning Officer, observers

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Representation of the People Act, 1951 — only Panchayat elections
Representation of the People Act, 1950 — corrupt practices and election petitions
Representation of the People Act, 1951 — allocation of seats and electoral rolls
Representation of the People Act, 1950 — electoral rolls and delimitation
accepted.x: The Representation of the People Act, 1950 deals with allocation of seats, delimitation and electoral rolls. The 1951 Act deals with the conduct of elections, corrupt practices and election petitions.
accepted.tq: Separate the administrative electoral-roll statute from the election-conduct statute.
accepted.sec: RPA 1950 vs RPA 1951 - subjects

accepted.s: Which of the following subjects is governed primarily by the Representation of the People Act, 1951?
o: Registration of political parties under Section 29A
Revision of electoral rolls under Section 21
accepted.x: Section 29A, concerning registration of political parties, belongs to the Representation of the People Act, 1951. Electoral-roll eligibility, roll revision, allocation of seats and delimitation are associated with the 1950 Act.
accepted.tq: Use the section number to identify the correct Act.
accepted.sec: RPA 1950 vs RPA 1951 - subjects

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Section 19, RPA 1950 — voter eligibility
2. Section 21, RPA 1950 — revision of electoral rolls
3. Section 8, RPA 1951 — disqualifications
4. Sections 77–78, RPA 1951 — election expense accounts
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched: Sections 19 and 21 belong to the 1950 Act, while Sections 8 and 77–78 belong to the 1951 Act.
accepted.tq: Verify each section-Act pairing before selecting the combined option.
accepted.sec: RPA 1950 vs RPA 1951 - subjects
